chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja'far from Ali ibn Hadid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who returns from his journey and the time for prayer has entered while he is on the road, so he said: 'He prays two rak'ahs. And if he departs for his journey and the time for prayer has entered, let him pray four.' And this report does not contradict what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for shortening prayers when returning from or departing on a journey?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise moment the legal status of 'traveler' (musafir) is established, distinguishing between the returnee who has already completed the journey and the departee who has not yet departed. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the ruling of qasr applies only after the traveler has left the city limits, whereas the one still within the city or just beginning the journey is considered a resident (muqim) and prays four rak'ahs. This distinction underscores the importance of intent and physical location in determining prayer length.
